papers.title: EXPERIMENTAL BURR ANALYSIS FOR TI-6AL-4V DRILLING APPLICATION
papers.abstract: To improve aerostructures assembly processes, aircraft manufacturers want to implement a One-Way Assembly strategy that eliminates the disassembly, cleaning and deburring phases currently required. Implementing this innovative strategy represents major technical challenges, including the management of burr formation at stack interfaces, as they have a negative impact on the assemblies’ fatigue strength. Despite extensive research, the burr formation phenomenon remains poorly understood. This paper presents an interrupted experimental design to investigate the burr formation during the drilling process of Ti-6Al-4V alloy. Analysis of burr geometry and microstructures is complemented by cutting force results for three different drilling tool geometries.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文研究Ti-6Al-4V钻孔毛刺形成，不涉及增材制造，因此与本方向（增材制造Ti-6Al-4V力学与疲劳）无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper studies burr formation during conventional drilling of Ti-6Al-4V, not additive manufacturing, so it does not address LPBF/SLM/EBM/DED mechanical or fatigue performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善航空装配中毛刺对疲劳强度的影响，推动单向装配策略。
summary_zh.method: 采用中断实验设计，分析三种钻头几何下的毛刺几何、微观结构和切削力。
summary_zh.result: 揭示了钻头几何对毛刺形成的影响，但未涉及增材制造。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验切削力与毛刺测量验证。

summary_en.motivation: To mitigate burr-induced fatigue reduction in aerospace assembly and enable one-way assembly strategy.
summary_en.method: An interrupted experimental design with three drill geometries was used to analyze burr geometry, microstructure, and cutting forces during Ti-6Al-4V drilling.
summary_en.result: Drill geometry significantly influences burr formation, but no additive manufacturing context is provided.
summary_en.validation: Experimental cutting force measurements and burr characterization validate the findings.

papers.title: IMPACT OF CRYOGENIC MILLING ON TOOL LIFE AND SURFACE INTEGRITY
papers.abstract: The machining of titanium alloys is associated with high temperature levels which result in rapid tool wear and poor surface integrity. To overcome this issue, cooling the cutting zone has emerged as a solution. This study evaluates the impact of different cooling/lubrication techniques on tool life, tool wear, and surface integrity during the milling of Ti-6Al-4V. The results show that using LCO2 and MQL extends tool life by factors of 2.4 and 2.9, respectively, compared to conventional flood cooling. These techniques also improve the surface quality of the machined parts.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文研究的是传统铣削冷却技术对工具寿命和表面完整性的影响，与增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not involve additive manufacturing or any post-processing treatment of AM Ti-6Al-4V; it focuses on conventional machining cooling techniques.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估不同冷却润滑技术对钛合金铣削的影响
summary_zh.method: 实验对比多种冷却润滑方式在Ti-6Al-4V铣削中的应用
summary_zh.result: LCO2和MQL分别使刀具寿命延长2.4和2.9倍，提高表面质量
summary_zh.validation: 通过刀具寿命和表面完整性实验验证

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to evaluate the impact of various cooling/lubrication techniques on tool life and surface integrity during milling of Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Experimental comparison of liquid CO2, minimum quantity lubrication, and conventional flood cooling during Ti-6Al-4V milling.
summary_en.result: LCO2 and MQL extended tool life by factors of 2.4 and 2.9, respectively, and improved surface quality.
summary_en.validation: Validation through experimental measurements of tool wear and surface roughness.
